root_motivation: **Who:** an autonomous coding agent calling a side-effecting tool on mcphost. **What:** a way to say 'this is the same request as before' so a retry after a timeout cannot execute the side effect twice.
user_persona: An agent whose tool call timed out; the error names _meta.idempotency_key, it retries with the same key and receives the stored result.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given 20 fake-mode persona sessions whose planted tool answers `tool_timeout` with the R6 hint, When each persona retries, Then >= 10 retries carry the same `idempotency_key` (falsifier).

Given a keyed call that succeeded, When the same key and args arrive 1 s later, Then the response equals the first byte-for-byte except `_meta.replayed: true` and the kind's call counter is unchanged.
Given a keyed call, When the same key arrives with different args, Then the code is `idempotency_conflict` and `data` carries both hashes.
Given two concurrent calls with the same key, When both complete, Then the tool ran exactly once and both responses carry the same result.

scope: src/idempotency.rs (new): key extraction, args hash, call_results claim/finish, ClaimGuard.
src/handler.rs: call_tool claims the key before dispatch, replays, stores, annotates tool_timeout.
non_goals: Declaring which tools are idempotent; caching by args alone; polling a running call; docs/llms.txt Idempotency paragraph (R7) and plan-ceiling accounting (R8).

additional.token_never_stored: only sha256(token) is stored; the token is shown once by the dry run.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can a retry after a timeout run a side effect twice?
five_whys_trace.a: No request identity reaches dispatch and no result is stored; the timeout error offers no next step.
